A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G3Flow study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original robotic manipulation simulations, success rates, computational efficiency measurements, and semantic-field comparisons in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a visual foundation model ablation in Section 4.5 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The proposed digital-twin construction, DINOv2/PCA features, FoundationPose tracking, diffusion policy, and training loss remain unchanged. CLIP and SAM are introduced as experimental replacement variants, without revising the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five RoboTwin tasks and terminal-control and cross-object evaluation scenarios, with matching object sets and Appendix A descriptions. The new VFM ablation reuses Shoe Place (T); articulated-object manipulation is mentioned only as future work.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates G3Flow with CLIP and SAM feature extractors against the DINOv2 implementation. Existing DP, DP3, colored DP3, scene-level feature, and D3Fields/GenDP comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds an experimental control varying the feature extractor on Shoe Place (T). Existing splits, demonstration counts, training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged. The five-dimensional PCA and 1024-point settings newly repeated in Section 4.1 were already documented in v2 Appendix B.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused ablation asking whether DINOv2, CLIP, or SAM provides better features for Shoe Place (T). The earlier efficiency, semantic-field quality, occlusion illustrations, and task visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds, 100 test episodes per seed, and success-rate means and standard deviations. v3 repeats the statistical explanation in Tables 1–2 captions and follows the existing uncertainty format in Table 5; no changed statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds success rates of 72.3±2.4 for G3Flow with CLIP and 74.7±5.0 with SAM, alongside the retained DINOv2 result of 83.0±3.6 on Shoe Place (T). Numerical results in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The observation definitions, pose transformation in Equation 1, denoising formulation in Equation 2, and loss in Equation 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction newly advertises an occlusion-robust representation using only a single-view camera, contrasting it with prior methods' multi-view requirements. This changes the stated positioning, although Section 3 still describes active multi-view initialization. The principal contributions and headline success-rate claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 4.5 attributes CLIP's weaker performance to image-text alignment and SAM's to excessive fine-detail emphasis. It extends the interpretation to generalization despite reporting only Shoe Place (T). The conclusion also shifts future directions toward articulated objects and continuing 3D-model refinement.

D1.justification: Disclosure is slightly reduced: v3 omits the explicitly unloaded GPU condition for timing measurements and the description of projecting RGB onto points for colored DP3. Appendix B's code and hyperparameters and the project link remain unchanged; the main-text PCA and point-count details duplicate the earlier appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds the AVR citation in Section 3.2 and specifies manual keypoint selection and multi-view field generation in its comparison with D3Fields/GenDP. The DexHandDiff/DexDiffuser reference is a bibliographic update to the matched work, rather than a new comparator.

P1.justification: Selected passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, ablation discussion, and conclusion are condensed or rewritten. v3 adds a VFM subsection, acknowledgements, an affiliation, and a supplementary-material heading, while retaining the overall section sequence and most method exposition.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised and corrects the reversed assignment of performance plots to terminal-control and generalization headings. v3 adds Table 5, relocates existing displays, expands several captions, and reformats the appendix opening. The remaining illustrations and overall layout style are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 1's misleading task-to-plot assignment and adds useful evidence supporting the DINOv2 feature choice, while preserving earlier results and implementation appendices. These are limited gains: the new ablation covers only Shoe Place (T), so its broader generalization and mechanism interpretations exceed what that comparison alone establishes.
